Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Creative Group Facilitator, Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Team,
I recently came across your Creative Group Facilitator opening and wanted to introduce myself. I understand the position may have been filled, but I would welcome consideration for this or future opportunities with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

My background brings together adolescent behavioral health support, recovery group facilitation, visual arts education, and fitness and wellness programming. 

At Family Center for Recovery, I supported adolescents and adults in structured treatment settings. At Futures Recovery Healthcare, I facilitated recovery support groups and helped alumni connect with resources and coping strategies. More recently, as an art teacher, I have designed creative activities that encourage confidence, expression, and engagement.

I am especially drawn to opportunities to help young people strengthen self-esteem and positive self-talk through art, movement, drama-inspired expression, and mindfulness. My approach values practical DBT-informed skills and creative activities as complements to the work of licensed treatment professionals.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my experience might support your programming. I have attached my resume for your consideration. 

Thank you for your time.

Warm regards, Jennifer Winston

candidates.cover_letter:
Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position leading the launch of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s first North Carolina clinic. As a licensed clinical social work and case management leader with more than 15 years of experience across behavioral health, healthcare, higher education, and community services, I offer the clinical supervision, operational leadership, and change-management experience needed to build a strong program from the ground up. AWA’s opportunity to create a focused, family-centered PHP/IOP clinic for adolescents is especially compelling to me because it combines direct clinical impact with the chance to shape culture, quality, and sustainable growth from day one.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. These experiences would enable me to recruit and develop clinicians, establish clear clinical and documentation standards, guide level-of-care decisions, and build trusted relationships with families and referral partners across North Carolina.

I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. My Master of Social Work and ongoing Doctor of Social Work studies in leadership further support my ability to connect evidence-informed clinical practice with disciplined operations and organizational growth.

AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.
Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

candidates.cover_letter:
I'm a Certified Behavioral Health Case Manager, with a Psychology degree from the University of Miami, and over three years of experience handling clinical file audits, insurance authorizations, and case management. I’d love to help keep your clients' care moving without delays as your company's new Utilization Review Specialist.

Right now, I work as a Housing Program Coordinator and Case Manager at Lotus House. My day-to-day is a mix of direct client support such as helping individuals manage depression and stabilize their health to heavy administrative review. I manage a high-volume caseload, verify Medicaid and Medicare coverage, run LOCUS risk assessments to track progress over time, and proactively audit clinical documentation to catch missing criteria before it leads to service or authorization delays. When denials do happen, I help clients and care teams navigate the gaps.

Before Lotus House, I worked remotely as a Compliance and Document Review Specialist for Miami-Dade County’s Emergency Rental Assistance Program, reviewing high-stakes applications against strict policy rules under tight deadlines. Between that, my research work at University of Miami, and daily EHR/HMIS tracking, I’m comfortable managing my own queue and staying organized while working remotely.

I’m familiar with DSM-5 and ASAM/LOCUS criteria, and I know how important clear, timely communication between clinical staff and insurance payers is for keeping treatment on track. Thank you so much for considering my application - I’d welcome the chance to talk more about how I can support your team!

Lindsey Duran

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position with your PHP and IOP programs. As an art educator, experienced teacher, and graduate student in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a specialization in Play Therapy, I have built my career around exactly what this role describes: using creative, process-based experiences to help young people express themselves, regulate their emotions, and discover their own capacity to grow.

Over the past couple of years, I have taught process-based art to children and adolescents in a variety of settings. At artNEST Studios, I facilitated weekly after-school art programs for elementary students, designing curriculum that intentionally prioritized creative exploration over the final product. This approach gives participants permission to take risks, make mistakes, and express themselves authentically. I also managed full-cycle logistics for camps, workshops, and parties, adapting programming in real time to different group dynamics, ability levels, and unexpected challenges while maintaining safety standards. These experiences taught me how to read the room, keep a group engaged, and create a warm, inclusive environment where participants feel safe to participate fully.

My work extends beyond the art studio into clinical and crisis contexts. I served as a Volunteer Crisis Counselor with The Trevor Project, providing culturally competent crisis support to LGBTQ+ youth, and I currently volunteer with Harmonia, where my training in crisis de-escalation, harm reduction, and trauma-informed care allows me to provide on-site emotional support to individuals experiencing acute psychological distress.

What draws me most to AWA is the belief that growth happens through connection, creativity, and kindness. I have seen firsthand how a safe space to create can open the door to emotional expression for young people who struggle to put their feelings into words. I would be honored to bring my experience in art facilitation, group management, and trauma-informed support to adolescents in your program, and I can offer consistent weekly or biweekly availability for on-site groups.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my creative practice and clinical training can contribute to your organization.

Warm regards,
Natalia Perez

My name is Corey Ann, and I’m the founder of Gypsy Jasmine Wellness. I’m a wellness practitioner with a background in yoga, personal training, mindful movement, and holistic wellness. My approach integrates movement, breathwork, somatic practices, fascia release, and mindfulness to support the mind-body connection and promote overall well-being.

Through my work, I aim to create welcoming, accessible experiences that help individuals reduce stress, reconnect with their bodies, improve mobility, cultivate self-awareness, and develop practical tools for navigating life's challenges.

My offerings include yoga, yoga nidra, guided relaxation, somatic movement, breathwork, fascia release, mobility, wellness coaching, and customized workshops and group experiences. I enjoy adapting my approach to meet the unique needs of different populations and environments.

My own journey with chronic pain and recovery has shaped my passion for this work and strengthened my belief in the importance of compassionate, individualized wellness support. I strive to create spaces where people feel supported, empowered, and encouraged to explore their own path toward greater well being.

I would welcome the opportunity to connect, learn more about your organization, and explore how my experience and offerings might complement your existing programs.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of connecting!

October 28, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

Dear Hiring Committee, 

Thank you for taking the time to review my resume and cover letter. I am writing to express my enthusiasm for the opportunity to continue my experience working as a Registered Mental Health Counseling Intern at  Adolescent Wellness Academy. I received a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and am a recent graduate with my Masters in Mental Health Counseling from the University of Miami. 

As a motivated and compassionate clinician, I am interested in expanding my experience of working with evidence-based treatment modalities. 

My educational experiences have helped me to build my knowledge and experience for working as a registered mental health counseling intern. I have a strong academic background in psychology, as well as a strong interest in working with children and their families to address mental health challenges at an early age, including Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Anxiety, and Depression. Through my recent experiences working as a practicum intern at Nicklaus Children’s Hospital and the Institute for Individual and Family Counseling, I was able to establish a strong foundation in conceptualizing cases, applying interventions and building rapport. 

In my previous experience working at Florida International University’s Summer Treatment Program, I had the opportunity to work directly with children and their families, providing support in areas such as emotional regulation, coping skills, and behavioral management. These experiences have provided a good foundation in implementing therapeutic strategies tailored to the unique needs of young children, as well as solidified my interest in child and adolescent mental health. 

I have a passion for working with programs that help to provide low-cost services for a diverse population, as highlighted in my experience working as a practicum intern at the institute for Individual and Family Counseling. I believe that my strong communication skills and dedication will allow for a wonderful learning experience as I continue my work in the field of mental health counseling.

Respectfully,

Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

I am writing to express my interest in opportunities with your organization as a Registered LCDC Intern or in

their own path forward.

people, training and mentoring teams, resolving difficult problems and communicating clearly. My
experience in special education reinforced the importance of adapting to individual needs, while my
customer-facing and leadership roles taught me the value of patience, accountability, confidentiality and
collaboration.
I recognize that lived experience is not a substitute for clinical training. I am eager to learn from experienced
counselors, develop evidence-based skills, respect professional boundaries and complete the supervised
experience required for full LCDC licensure. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute in an entry-level
capacity while growing as a counselor.
Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background,
commitment to recovery services and willingness to learn could contribute to your organization.
Sincerely,
Jason Leggett

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and professional experience in case management, client support, and relationship building, I bring a strong foundation in compassionate communication, problem-solving, and helping individuals and families navigate sensitive and sometimes challenging situations.

In my previous role as a Case Manager at Antioch Adoptions, I worked closely with families throughout an emotionally significant and often complex process. My responsibilities included conducting interviews and evaluations, managing sensitive client cases, maintaining detailed documentation, and coordinating communication between families, DCYF, and internal teams. This position followed a hybrid work schedule, allowing me to develop experience balancing remote and in-person responsibilities while maintaining organization, communication, and productivity. This experience strengthened my ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and provide consistent support to clients.

In addition to my professional background, I bring a personal understanding of the importance of compassionate, patient-centered mental health care. This perspective has given me a deeper appreciation for the vulnerability individuals and families may experience when seeking treatment and the difference that supportive, empathetic communication can make during that process. I would bring this understanding to every interaction, helping individuals feel heard, respected, and supported as they take the first steps toward receiving care.

I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming experience for individuals and their families. I would approach every interaction with patience, compassion, and a genuine desire to make the admissions process feel more approachable. I am comfortable handling sensitive conversations, managing multiple priorities, maintaining accurate records, and communicating clearly with individuals from different backgrounds. My previous customer service experience has also strengthened my ability to resolve concerns, establish positive relationships, and provide a welcoming experience over the phone and in person.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to combine my background in psychology and case management with my passion for helping others. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to a team that makes accessing mental health and recovery services easier for individuals and families during some of their most difficult moments.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, communication skills, and commitment to compassionate client support could contribute to your admissions team. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,  
Jordan Bills

I believe adolescents deserve to be heard, understood, and supported without judgment. candidates.cover_letter:
November 17, 2026
Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center
Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. The opportunity to be a welcoming, steady first point of contact for individuals and families seeking behavioral health treatment is meaningful to me. Through my experience in ABA services, higher-education administration, and customer support, I have developed the communication, organization, and people-centered approach needed to help callers feel heard while ensuring that important details and next steps are handled responsibly.
In my current role as a Behavior Technician with Discovery ABA, I work directly with individuals with autism spectrum disorder, implement individualized behavior intervention plans, document client progress, and communicate observations with supervisors, care-team members, and families. My previous work with Compleat Kidz further strengthened my experience in a structured behavioral-health setting. These roles have taught me to remain patient, attentive, and professional when people have different needs and ways of communicating. They have also reinforced that behind every record, treatment goal, and conversation is a person who deserves dignity, consistency, and care.
My administrative experience at Hood Theological Seminary is also directly relevant to the coordination responsibilities of this position. I support admissions and administrative operations through prospective-student communication, records management, data entry, correspondence, and follow-up. I regularly respond to inquiries by phone, email, and in person, organize information, manage competing priorities, and handle sensitive information with discretion. I understand the importance of accurate documentation and timely follow-through so that individuals are not left wondering what happens next.
Earlier, as a Reservation Specialist with American Airlines, I developed confidence handling high-volume phone interactions, listening carefully to understand concerns, explaining processes, navigating established procedures, and working toward practical solutions. That experience strengthened my ability to communicate clearly and remain composed when someone needs assistance. I would bring that same attentiveness to conversations with prospective clients, parents, caregivers, and referral partners who may be reaching out during an especially difficult time.
I recognize that this role includes specialized admissions responsibilities such as insurance verification, coordinating clinical assessments, and documenting leads in CRM and EMR platforms. My experience has provided a strong foundation in behavioral-health services, admissions-related administrative support, documentation, and client communication; I am prepared to learn the specific systems and workflows used by your programs. I would approach those responsibilities with accuracy, accountability, respect for confidentiality, and a willingness to ask questions and follow established procedures.
My Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies and my ongoing Master of Arts in Chaplaincy reflect a longstanding commitment to understanding people and serving them with compassion. My approach is grounded in the belief that people should be treated with patience and respect, especially when they are navigating uncertainty. I would value the opportunity to bring that perspective, along with my professional experience and strong follow-through, to a team helping adolescents and adults take meaningful steps toward treatment and recovery.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral-health experience, administrative background, and commitment to compassionate service could contribute to your admissions team.
Sincerely,
Samuel Allen

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy, 
I'm excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with your company. The posting says many callers reach out on one of the hardest days of their lives. My clinical training was built for meeting people in those moments with compassion and guiding them toward a clear next step.
I hold a Masters degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Walden University, with an emphasis in eating disorders. During my internship at Turning Point Center for Youth, I worked directly with high-risk adolescents I learned to build trust quickly, ask the right questions without judgment, and stay steady when a conversation turned emotional. Those skills apply to AWA's teens and families, who often reach out in crisis.
My administrative background supports the operational side of the role. As an Implementation Coordinator at Integrated Listening Systems, I managed applications, agreements, and records, spoke with clients and therapists by phone to gather information and answer questions, coordinated details with accounting, and kept a company database accurate. In my own business, The Whole Nest, LLC, I use a CRM and EMR to track every client from first inquiry through follow-up, manage intake, and keep records accurate and organized, all remotely from my home. More recently, as a Home Care Worker at Wind Crest by Erickson Senior Living, I communicated with residents, families, and care teams to relay updates and keep care consistent.
You'll see a gap in my work history. I stepped away for many to be a stay-at-home parent to my three children, which deepened my patience and my understanding of what families go through when they're worried about their children. 
I'd welcome the chance to talk about how my counseling background, follow-through, and warm phone presence can support your admissions team. I also minored in Spanish and studied abroad in Seville, so I'm glad to support Spanish-speaking families. Thank you for your consideration.
Sincerely,
Callie Pedersen

Dear Hiring Manager,

Helping a family take a clear next step during a difficult moment calls for calm communication, careful listening, and dependable follow-through. I’m interested in bringing my admissions-support background, warm phone presence, and experience managing complex work independently to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s virtual admissions team.

At Indiana University East, I developed content and campaigns supporting Admissions and engaging prospective students, families, and other community members. That experience taught me to communicate clearly with people who have different questions and needs, and to collaborate across departments to make information accessible. I would bring the same thoughtful, audience-focused approach to explaining PHP and IOP options to teens and families and helping them understand what happens next.

As a creative marketing business owner, I manage multiple client projects from planning through delivery, coordinate with diverse stakeholders, and maintain consistent follow-through without daily direction. These responsibilities have strengthened my organization, relationship-building, and remote-work skills—qualities that translate directly to tracking inquiries, staying in touch with callers, and coordinating assessments and intake steps. My background also includes CRM systems, phone presence, and follow-through. I’m prepared to learn your specific CRM and EMR workflows and to handle sensitive information with care and attention to established privacy procedures.

My psychology studies at Indiana University East further inform my interest in supporting adolescents and families with respect and empathy. In collaborative community storytelling work, I’ve listened to people with varied perspectives and shaped their input into clear, cohesive narratives. That practice has reinforced the importance of patience, trust, and meeting each person where they are—especially when a conversation is personal.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my communication, admissions-related, and project-management strengths can support your team and help callers move toward care. Thank you for your consideration; I’d be glad to speak as you plan your upcoming admissions needs.
Best regards,
Julian Short

Dear Hiring Staff,


I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With direct experience in behavioral health admissions, residential treatment, and case management, I bring a strong combination of relevant industry knowledge, interpersonal communication skills, and a compassionate, solutions-oriented approach. 

In my previous role as a Behavioral Health Admissions Coordinator with Pasadena Villa Network and Clearview Treatment Centers, I guided individuals seeking residential behavioral health services through the admissions process, providing support and gathering essential information through assessments and clinical history reviews. My responsibilities included conducting comprehensive biopsychosocial assessments, gathering clinical histories, coordinating aftercare, and collaborating with families and professional providers. Having worked directly with individuals throughout their treatment experiences, I understand the importance of approaching prospective clients and their families with genuine empathy, patience, and professionalism.
I also hold dual bachelor's degrees in Psychology and English Literature from the University of Central Florida, graduating cum laude in both disciplines. My educational background complements my professional experience, providing a strong foundation in human behavior, critical thinking, and effective written and verbal communication.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to apply my existing behavioral health admissions experience in a remote setting while continuing to contribute to an important aspect of the treatment process. I recognize that the admissions process involves much more than gathering information and coordinating logistics; it is often a family's first meaningful interaction with a treatment provider. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, attentiveness, and commitment to compassionate care to your team.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its admissions team.

Sincerely,
Jeremiah Novak, B.A.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in joining your team in a remote position supporting individuals navigating mental health challenges, personal struggles, and difficult life transitions.

Helping people has always been more than a job to me; it is genuinely my passion. Throughout my experience, I have had the opportunity to work with women and families in shelters, individuals in recovery and rehabilitation homes, people requiring additional daily living support, youth involved with the Department of Children and Families (DCF), and teenagers experiencing homelessness or running away from home.

These experiences have given me a strong understanding of the importance of compassion, patience, active listening, emotional support, and meeting people where they are in life. I understand that sometimes people don’t need someone to judge them or tell them what to do. They need someone willing to listen, recognize their struggles, encourage their growth, and remind them that their circumstances do not define their future.

Beyond my professional experience, I am deeply passionate about personal development, emotional healing, and empowering women to recognize their strength and potential. Through my own life experiences, I have developed a genuine appreciation for resilience, overcoming adversity, and the importance of having someone in your corner. I enjoy encouraging others, helping them find perspective, and reminding them that healing and growth are possible.

I bring hands-on experience, strong interpersonal skills, empathy, adaptability, and a willingness to continuously learn. I am a quick learner, comfortable working with diverse populations, and confident in my ability to build rapport with individuals from different backgrounds and circumstances. I also understand the importance of professionalism, confidentiality, boundaries, and treating every individual with dignity and respect.

I would love the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and dedication to an organization that values making a meaningful difference in people’s lives. I am eager to continue growing professionally while doing work that aligns with something I have always been passionate about: helping others feel heard, supported, empowered, and capable of moving forward.

work_history.summary: A substitute teacher temporarily takes over the role of the regular classroom teacher when that teacher is absent. Substitute teachers can work on a day-to-day basis or for longer periods, sometimes even developing their own lesson plans for extended absences. work_history.company_name: Salem County Correction Facility Sheriff Department

They oversee inmate activities, including meals, recreation, and work programs, ensuring compliance with facility rules and regulations. Officers are responsible for enforcing rules and maintaining order within the facility, addressing any violations or disruptive behavior. They may be required to escort inmates between different areas of the facility, to court appearances, or to other correctional institution..Correctional officers document inmate behavior, incidents, and any relevant information related to the facility's operations. They inspect facilities for security and safety issues, such as contraband or hazards, and ensure that the facility meets required standards.

work_history.title: Parole Employment Coordinator
work_history.summary: A Parole Employment Coordinator works to help parolees find and maintain employment. This role involves coordinating job placement services, providing guidance on job readiness, and collaborating with employers to create opportunities for individuals transitioning back into the community after incarceration. They also work with parole officers and other community partners to support the parolee's successful reintegration. Connecting parolees with potential employers and job training programs.Assisting parolees with resume writing, interview skills, and other job search strategies.Working with parole officers, community organizations, and employers to create a supportive environment for employment.Maintaining records, tracking progress, and providing ongoing support to parolees.Ensuring parolees adhere to any employment-related conditions set by the parole board.A Parole Employment Coordinator might work with a local community college to enroll a parolee in a vocational training program, or partner with a staffing agency to find temporary employment opportunities. They would also work with the parole officer to ensure the parolee is meeting all requirements related to their parole, including those related to employment.

work_history.title: Parole Case Manager
work_history.summary: A parole case manager, also known as a correctional treatment specialist, is a professional who works within the criminal justice system to support individuals on parole. They develop and implement rehabilitation plans, monitor progress, and help parolees reintegrate into the community.Evaluate the needs of individuals on parole, including their criminogenic needs (factors that increase the risk of re-offending), and assess their ability to remain crime-free. Create individualized plans that address identified needs, often involving substance abuse treatment, job training, or other forms of support. Regularly track the progress of parolees, ensuring they are adhering to their plans and making positive changes. Offer counseling, resources, and assistance to parolees as they navigate the challenges of reintegration into the community. Work with parole officers, social workers, mental health professionals, and other agencies to provide comprehensive support. Responding to and managing crises or challenging situations that may arise during the parole period. Substitute Teacher

Hiring Manager

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Human and Community Advocacy from the University of Texas at San Antonio, an Associate of Arts in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare, customer service, and public assistance, I bring a combination of professional qualifications, compassion, and a genuine commitment to helping adolescents and families access mental health services.

Throughout my career, including my work with Texas Health and Human Services, healthcare-related call centers, and my current position with Aflac, I have developed strong skills in communication, active listening, documentation, problem-solving, and assisting individuals through complex and sometimes emotionally challenging situations. My experience has taught me the importance of maintaining confidentiality, gathering accurate information, explaining processes clearly, and ensuring that individuals feel respected and supported.

What makes this opportunity particularly meaningful to me is my personal experience as a mother who has navigated the mental health system while advocating for a child experiencing significant emotional and behavioral health challenges. I understand firsthand the fear, uncertainty, and emotional exhaustion that families can experience when trying to find appropriate treatment. My family has navigated hospitalizations, mental health crises, and community-based behavioral health services, including the YES Waiver program. Through those experiences, I witnessed how compassionate professionals can make an extraordinary difference in the lives of both adolescents and their families.

Those experiences strengthened my desire to pursue a career in mental health advocacy. They also taught me the importance of listening without judgment, communicating with empathy, and helping families feel supported during some of their most vulnerable moments. I recognize that an admissions coordinator may be one of the first people a struggling adolescent or concerned parent speaks with, and I would approach that responsibility with professionalism, patience, compassion, and respect.

I am particularly interested in the opportunity to assist families throughout the admissions process, coordinate necessary information, communicate with treatment teams, and help individuals better understand their options for care. My background in telephone-based customer service, healthcare documentation, insurance-related inquiries, and administrative support would allow me to contribute meaningfully while continuing to develop my knowledge of adolescent mental health and substance use treatment.

As I pursue my long-term goal of earning a Master of Social Work, I am seeking an opportunity where my professional skills and personal passion can come together to make a meaningful difference. I would be honored to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s work supporting adolescents and helping families find hope, guidance, and access to appropriate treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and dedication to mental health advocacy would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Jermiane Rodriguez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my professional background working in juvenile corrections and youth rehabilitation, I believe I can bring valuable experience, compassion, and a strong understanding of the challenges adolescents and their families face.

Through my work at Prairie Lakes Youth Programs, I have gained firsthand experience supporting young people facing behavioral challenges, difficult family circumstances, and significant obstacles in their lives. Working in this environment has taught me the importance of patience, effective communication, confidentiality, and treating every individual with dignity and respect.

One of the most meaningful parts of my work has been recognizing that behind every struggling young person is a story, and often a family searching for answers, guidance, and hope. I understand how important it is for families to feel heard, supported, and reassured when taking the first steps toward getting help.

I am comfortable navigating sensitive conversations, maintaining accurate documentation, handling challenging situations professionally, and working with individuals from many different backgrounds. I believe these skills would translate well into an admissions role where compassion, organization, and clear communication are essential.

I am particularly interested in Adolescent Wellness Academy because of its focus on helping young people access the treatment and support they need. I would welcome the opportunity to continue making a difference in the lives of adolescents while contributing to your admissions team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and dedication to helping young people could benefit your organization.

Sincerely,
Rikki Wold

I would appreciate the opportunity to bring my communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills to your team. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,

Emily Hoffman

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use. With an extensive professional background in behavioral health, substance use counseling, case management, and juvenile justice, I am passionate about connecting individuals and families with the resources, treatment, and support they need to achieve meaningful and lasting change.

I hold a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from Western Kentucky University, with minors in Nonprofit Administration and Clinical and Community Behavioral Health. My professional qualifications include certification as an Alcohol and Drug Counselor, International Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor, Targeted Case Manager, and Trauma-Informed Interviewer, as well as training in assessing and managing suicide risk.

Throughout my career, I have had the privilege of working with individuals and families navigating complex behavioral health challenges. My experience as a Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor, Targeted Case Manager, Youth Counselor, Court Designated Worker, and, most recently, Program Project Coordinator has strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, build rapport, identify individual needs, coordinate services, and collaborate with multidisciplinary professionals. I understand the importance of approaching each individual and family with compassion, empathy, professionalism, and a sense of urgency, particularly when seeking treatment during difficult and vulnerable circumstances.

I am a highly motivated self-starter who takes initiative, demonstrates accountability, and works exceptionally well independently. I possess strong organizational and time management skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively. My proficiency with technology, combined with my strong communication skills and commitment to maintaining confidentiality, makes me well-equipped to excel in a remote work environment without the need for constant supervision.

What draws me most to this opportunity is the ability to make a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents and their families. I recognize that the admissions process is often the first step toward healing and recovery, and I would welcome the opportunity to provide families with a compassionate, knowledgeable, and reassuring experience as they navigate that journey.

I am confident that my combination of clinical experience, administrative expertise, independent work ethic, and genuine passion for helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, qualifications, and dedication align with the needs and mission of your organization.

Sincerely,
Angela Johnson

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology and hands-on experience in substance use treatment admissions, behavioral health support, insurance-related customer service, and confidential clinical documentation, I bring the combination of compassion, accuracy, and follow-through needed to guide individuals and families through a sensitive first step toward care.

As a Clinical Intake Specialist at Icarus Alcohol & Drug Rehab, I collected and documented intake information, entered clinical and administrative details into electronic medical records, and coordinated with clients and internal teams regarding documentation, scheduling, and next steps. I did the interviews with patients in person and virtually using the Kipu system. I dealt with people in sensitive moments in their life with empathy; helping them through the entire process. My earlier work as a Behavioral Health Technician gave me direct insight into the importance of respectful communication, timely progress notes, privacy, and collaboration with clinical staff. Together, these experiences prepared me to speak with people seeking treatment in a calm, supportive, and organized way.

I also bring benefits verification and high-volume phone support experience from C3 Customer Contact Channels, along with strong records management and family communication skills developed in education and child-focused roles. I understand that an admissions coordinator must do more than answer an inquiry: each person needs clear information, reliable follow-up, accurate records, and a thoughtful handoff. I am comfortable working across digital systems and maintaining HIPAA-conscious documentation while keeping the caller’s needs at the center of every interaction.

Commitment to helping adolescents, families, and adults access mental health and substance use treatment is especially meaningful to me. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my intake background, attention to detail, and empathetic communication style to your virtual admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how I can support your programs and the people who reach out for help.

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I enjoy being the person families can turn to when they know they need help and are trying to figure out where to start. This role brings together the work I’ve done in behavioral health intake, insurance verification, and supporting people seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as an Eligibility Specialist, I verify benefits, review documentation, and help families work through coverage issues that could delay care. Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to bring my bilingual communication skills, intake experience, and follow-through to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Stephany Bhisham

Christen Estep, RMHCI

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining your organization. As a Licensed Mental Health Counselor in Florida with over 10 years of experience in behavioral health, I bring a strong background in clinical quality assurance, compliance, clinical leadership, and direct patient care. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical information, make sound decisions, and support both clinicians and organizational objectives.

I am particularly interested in opportunities where I can apply my clinical knowledge, analytical skills, and commitment to quality to support effective behavioral health services. As a bilingual professional fluent in English and Spanish, I also bring the ability to communicate effectively with diverse populations and multidisciplinary teams.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Melissa Ortega, LMHC

candidates.cover_letter:
Abigail Cornele
910-330-5752
acornele42@gmail.com
11/11/26

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Mooresville, NC

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker Associate (LCSWA) with a Master of Social Work degree and three years of experience supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to AWA's mission of providing compassionate, evidence-based mental health services to adolescents. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to join the founding clinical team and help establish a supportive, collaborative, and client-centered therapeutic environment.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong foundation in family-centered treatment, crisis intervention, case management, treatment planning, and trauma-informed care. In my current role as a Family Centered Treatment Specialist with Pinnacle Family Services, I provide individualized treatment and case management services to children and families in home and community settings. I develop treatment plans, facilitate interventions, collaborate with community partners, and support families in navigating challenges while promoting stability, resilience, and improved outcomes. This experience has strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, identify individual and family needs, and implement interventions that support meaningful behavioral and emotional change.

Previously, as a Family Advocate at Pat's Place Child Advocacy Center, I supported children and families navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. I provided emotional support, crisis intervention, resource coordination, and advocacy while collaborating with multidisciplinary professionals to prioritize child safety and family well-being. My school social work experience at Hawthorne Academy further strengthened my ability to recognize and address the emotional, behavioral, academic, and social needs of at-risk students while developing interventions and connecting families with appropriate resources.

I believe my background in child and family services provides a valuable foundation for working with adolescents experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, behavioral challenges, and other mental health concerns. I am passionate about creating a therapeutic space where adolescents feel safe, understood, and empowered to develop healthy coping strategies and recognize their strengths. I also understand the importance of family involvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, individualized treatment planning, and consistent communication in supporting successful clinical outcomes.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, dedication to family-centered care, and passion for adolescent mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Being part of a new program would allow me to contribute not only to the care of adolescents and their families but also to the development of a positive clinical culture built on compassion, collaboration, and excellence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and commitment to serving children and families would make me a valuable addition to AWA's founding clinical team.

Sincerely,

Abigail Cornele, MSW, LCSWA

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in the Operations Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy as you prepare to open your first North Carolina clinic. What excites me most about this opportunity is the chance to be part of something that can make a genuine difference in the lives of young people and their families. Throughout my career, I have found the most rewarding part of my work is knowing that what I do has a meaningful impact on someone else's life. That is something I experienced firsthand at Shine Support Services, and it is something I hope to continue in my next role.

At Shine Support Services, I helped build the Supportive Employment Program from the ground up. I operated and developed workflows, internal procedures, training materials, participant resources, and documentation standards to help establish the foundation for daily operations. More importantly, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, support their goals, and build relationships with their families and community partners. I loved being able to see the difference that consistent support and encouragement could make in someone's confidence, independence, and everyday life. I taught a coping skills class that incorporated Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) practices, giving participants the opportunity to learn and practice healthy coping strategies. Those experiences reminded me that meaningful progress is not always one big milestone. Sometimes it is the smaller moments of growth that make the work so worthwhile.

I also bring leadership and operational experience from Graphic Components, where I led the photopolymer department before being promoted to Project Manager. I coordinated departmental workflow, monitored quality, addressed production challenges, developed procedures and training documentation, and cross-trained employees and prospective hires. This experience strengthened my ability to organize competing priorities, support a team, solve problems, and create systems that help people do their jobs effectively.

My experience working with young people also extends to YPATC, a youth performing arts program in Florida, where my responsibilities ranged from scheduling appointments to teaching theater to children. I enjoyed being part of an environment where I could contribute both behind the scenes and directly to the experiences of young people. I have pursued the 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training coursework, further developing my understanding of behavioral support and different learning and support needs.

What draws me to AWA is the opportunity to bring these experiences together in a setting where the work has such an important purpose. I understand that a successful program depends on more than the services being offered. It also takes thoughtful organization, dependable staff, clear communication, consistent routines, and an environment where young people and their families feel supported. I would be excited to help build that foundation for AWA's North Carolina clinic.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, leadership, and passion for meaningful work could contribute to AWA's founding North Carolina team.

Sincerely,

Erica R. Warriner

Committed to helping youth and adults build independence while maintaining a welcoming and respectful environment. CORE QUALIFICATIONS Youth Mentorship * Life Skills Development * Resident Support * Peer Support * Community Resource Navigation * Confidential Documentation * Records Management * Customer Service * Team Collaboration * Microsoft Office

work_history.title: Peer Specialist
work_history.summary: Welcomed participants, responded to questions, and provided compassionate support in a behavioral health setting. Maintained timely, confidential documentation and coordinated with multidisciplinary teams to support continuity of care. Scheduled participant activities and connected individuals with housing, employment, transportation, and healthcare resources. Facilitated peer groups while maintaining professional boundaries and a respectful service environment.

work_history.title: Residential Coordinator
work_history.summary: Assisted residents with questions and concerns while maintaining a welcoming and respectful residential environment. Coordinated resident activities and provided information about available community services and resources. Maintained resident records and documentation while protecting confidential information. Communicated with residents, staff, and service providers to support resident needs and daily operations.

work_history.title: Youth Skills Coach
work_history.summary: Supported youth in developing daily living skills, setting personal goals, and building independence. Provided mentorship and encouragement to help youth strengthen communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Helped youth prepare for greater responsibility through practical life-skills activities and individual support.
